q: In read/write compaction, what does the slow pointer k mean?
options: The number of kept elements so far = where the next kept one goes
why: nums[0..k-1] is the finished part. The next value you keep is written at index k.

q: After this runs on nums = [1, 1, 2, 3, 3], what is k?
why: The unique values 1, 2, 3 end up in nums[0..2].

q: Removing all zeros by calling `nums.remove(0)` in a loop costs…
why: Each remove shifts everything after it: O(n) per call. Read/write pointers do it in one O(n) pass.

q: Sort Colors: after swapping nums[mid] with nums[hi], why doesn't mid move?
options: The value swapped in from hi hasn't been examined yet
why: The region [mid, hi] is unknown. The swapped-in value came from that region, so it still needs checking.

q: "Is s a subsequence of t?" Best approach?
options: One pointer in each string, advance in s only on a match
why: Greedy matching: take each character of s at its earliest spot in t. O(len(t)) time, O(1) space.

q: What is nums after this, starting from [0, 1, 0, 3, 12]?
why: Each non-zero is swapped to the next write slot, so non-zeros keep their order and zeros drift to the end.
